items.title: Countable canonical model
items.design_state: Draft definition carrier recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty finite or countably infinite set equipped with a specified enumeration, let $E_i\in\mathbb R$ be finite energies, let $g_i>0$ be weights, and let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open parameter interval. For a nonnegative family $(a_i)_{i\in I}$ define $\sum_{i\in I}a_i:=\sup_{F\subset I,\,F\text{ finite}}\sum_{i\in F}a_i$, with finite sums as in [[def-finite-sum]] and the supremum as in [[def-complete-ordered-field]] when the finite subsums are bounded; set the value to $+\infty$ when they are unbounded. This definition is independent of the specified enumeration. For $\beta\in J$, define the nonnegative partition sum $Z(\beta):=\sum_{i\in I}g_i\exp(-\beta E_i)$ by this rule. The admissible parameter set is $J_Z:=\{\beta\in J:0<Z(\beta)<\infty\}$. For $\beta\in J_Z$, define $p_i(\beta):=g_i\exp(-\beta E_i)/Z(\beta)$. A countable probability law on $I$ means a nonnegative family with total sum $1$ under the finite-subsum convention above; these weights form such a law because $\sum_i p_i(\beta)=Z(\beta)/Z(\beta)=1$. For any real family $X_i$ with $\sum_i p_i|X_i|<\infty$, define $\langle X\rangle_\beta:=\sum_i p_iX_i$. If $\sum_i|p_i\log(p_i/g_i)|<\infty$, define the reference-relative entropy $H_g(p):=-\sum_i p_i\log(p_i/g_i)$. When $g_i=1$, this is the Shannon entropy with natural logarithms. A lower bound on the energies alone is not part of this definition and does not imply $Z(\beta)<\infty$. For countably infinite $I$, any specified enumeration is used only to write a list; the nonnegative sum itself is the supremum over finite subsums above.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete numbered argument is in items/def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Summable canonical differentiation
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let $I,E_i,g_i,J,Z$ be as in [[def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model]]. Suppose that for every compact interval $K\subset J$ there is a summable sequence $a_i\ge0$ such that $g_i(1+|E_i|^2)\exp(-\beta E_i)\le a_i$ for every $i\in I$ and $\beta\in K$. Then $Z$ is positive, finite, and $C^2$ on $J$, with $Z'(\beta)=-\sum_i g_iE_i\exp(-\beta E_i)$ and $Z''(\beta)=\sum_i g_iE_i^2\exp(-\beta E_i)$. The probabilities $p_i$ are normalized. Define $\bar E:=\langle E\rangle_\beta$ and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E):=\sum_i p_i(E_i-\bar E)^2$. These quantities are finite and satisfy $-\partial_\beta\log Z=\bar E$ and $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$. Moreover $H_g(p)=\log Z+\beta\bar E$, and its defining series is absolutely convergent.

items.title: Diagonal self-adjoint operator model
items.design_state: Draft definition carrier recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let $I$ be a finite or countably infinite set with a specified enumeration, let $E_i\in\mathbb R$, and let $\ell^2(I):=\{x:I\to\mathbb C:\sum_i|x_i|^2<\infty\}$ with inner product $\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_i x_i\overline{y_i}$, linear in the first variable. Write $u_i$ for the coordinate unit vector at $i$. The diagonal multiplication operator $H_E$ is the linear operator with domain $D(H_E):=\{x\in\ell^2(I):\sum_i|E_ix_i|^2<\infty\}$ and action $(H_Ex)_i:=E_ix_i$. [[lem-tdmath-diagonal-model-hilbert-and-domain]] proves completeness of the coefficient space, linearity and density of this domain, and linearity of the coordinate action before the Hilbert-space operator interpretation is used. Its domain is part of the operator data in the sense of [[def-unbounded-linear-operator-domain-and-graph]].

items.statement: For the finite or explicitly enumerated countable index set $I$ of [[def-tdmath-diagonal-operator-model]], the inner-product space $\ell^2(I)$ is complete and therefore a complex Hilbert space, with inner product linear in the first variable. For any real family $(E_i)$, the displayed domain $D(H_E)$ is a linear subspace containing every finite-support vector, is dense in $\ell^2(I)$, and $x\mapsto(E_ix_i)_i$ is a linear map from that domain into $\ell^2(I)$. These assertions also hold for the empty finite index set.

items.title: Measure space and integral
items.design_state: Draft definition carrier recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: A measure space is a triple $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ where $\Sigma$ contains $\varnothing,X$ and is closed under complements and countable unions (a $\sigma$-algebra) of subsets of $X$ and $\mu:\Sigma\to[0,\infty]$ is countably additive with $\mu(\varnothing)=0$. A measurable function $f:X\to[-\infty,\infty]$ has measurable inverse images of Borel sets, where $[-\infty,\infty]$ has its order topology: finite open intervals and the endpoint neighborhoods $[-\infty,a)$ and $(a,\infty]$ form a basis. Its Borel sigma-algebra is generated by these open sets. A complex-valued function is measurable exactly when its finite real and imaginary parts are measurable, equivalently for the usual Borel structure of $\mathbb C$. Almost-everywhere assertions mean outside a measurable $\mu$-null set; completeness of $\mu$ is not assumed. Nonnegative extended addition uses $a+\infty=\infty+a=\infty$ for $a\in[0,\infty]$; positive scalars multiply $\infty$ to $\infty$, while $0\cdot\infty=0$. Signed expressions $\infty-\infty$ remain undefined and are not used in signed integrals. A nonnegative simple function has the form $s=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\mathbf1_{A_j}$ with finitely many disjoint $A_j\in\Sigma$ and finite $c_j\ge0$. Define $c\mu(A)=+\infty$ if $c>0$ and $\mu(A)=+\infty$, define $0\cdot\infty:=0$, and define the finite sum of these extended nonnegative terms to be $+\infty$ if any term is $+\infty$ and otherwise the real finite sum of [[def-finite-sum]]. Then $\int s\,d\mu:=\sum_j c_j\mu(A_j)$; using canonical level sets $\{s=c\}$ makes this value representation-independent. For measurable $f\ge0$, define $\int f\,d\mu:=\sup\{\int s\,d\mu: s\text{ is simple and }0\le s\le f\}$, using [[def-complete-ordered-field]] for a bounded set of finite values and setting the supremum to $+\infty$ when the values are unbounded or one is infinite. A real measurable $f$ is integrable when $\int|f|\,d\mu<\infty$, and then $\int f:=\int f^+-\int f^-$, where $f^+=\max(f,0)$ and $f^-:=\max(-f,0)$. Complex integrability and integration are defined by integrable real and imaginary parts.

items.title: Monotone convergence for the measure integral
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $f_n:X\to[0,\infty]$ be measurable with $f_n\le f_{n+1}$ and $f_n\to f$ pointwise. Then $\int f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int f\,d\mu$, including infinite values. Also, for measurable $f,g\ge0$, $\int(f+g)\,d\mu=\int f\,d\mu+\int g\,d\mu$. For every $c\ge0$, $\int cf\,d\mu=c\int f\,d\mu$; the integral is also linear on real integrable functions.

items.title: Dominated convergence for the measure integral
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $f_n:X\to\mathbb C$ be measurable with $f_n\to f$ almost everywhere. Suppose $g\ge0$ is measurable and $\int g\,d\mu<\infty$, and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for every $n$. Let $f_0(x)$ be the finite complex pointwise limit of $(f_n(x))$ where it exists, and $0$ elsewhere. Then $f_0$ is measurable, equals $f$ almost everywhere, is integrable, and $\int f_n\,d\mu\to\int f_0\,d\mu$ and $\int|f_n-f_0|\,d\mu\to0$. If the specified $f$ is measurable, these same conclusions hold with $f$ in place of $f_0$. In particular this is automatic when $\mu$ is complete. On a noncomplete measure space an arbitrary almost-everywhere representative need not be measurable, so no integral of such a nonmeasurable $f$ is asserted.

items.title: Measurable canonical normalization and identities
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $E:X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $Z(\beta):=\int e^{-\beta E}\,d\mu$ satisfies $0<Z(\beta)<\infty$ on $J$, and for every compact interval $K\subset J$ there is $G_K\in L^1(\mu)$ with $(1+|E|^2)e^{-\beta E}\le G_K$ pointwise for every $\beta\in K$. Define $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z(\beta)$, $\langle Y\rangle_\beta:=\int Yp_\beta\,d\mu$ for integrable $Y$, and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E):=\int(E-\langle E\rangle_\beta)^2p_\beta\,d\mu$. Then $Z\in C^2(J)$, $Z'=-\int E e^{-\beta E}d\mu$, $Z''=\int E^2e^{-\beta E}d\mu$, and $-\partial_\beta\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta$, $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$. The reference-relative entropy $-\int p_\beta\log p_\beta\,d\mu$ is finite and equals $\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta$.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete numbered argument is in items/thm-tdmath-measurable-canonical-identities.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Finite-bath canonical error bound
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let $I$ be a finite nonempty subsystem state set, let $E_i\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|E_i|\le L$ for $L\ge0$, and let the dimensionless bath entropy $s_B$ be $C^2$ on an open interval $U$ containing $[u_0-L,u_0+L]$, with $|s_B''(u)|\le M$ on that closed interval for $M\ge0$. Use one energy unit for $E_i,u_0,L$, so $\beta=s_B'(u_0)$ has inverse-energy units and $M$ has inverse-energy-squared units; $\delta=ML^2/2$ is dimensionless. Put $Z:=\sum_{j\in I}e^{-\beta E_j}$ and $q_i:=e^{-\beta E_i}/Z$. Suppose the joint shell weights induce the normalized subsystem law $p_i:=e^{s_B(u_0-E_i)}/\sum_{j\in I}e^{s_B(u_0-E_j)}$. Then $|s_B(u_0-E_i)-s_B(u_0)+\beta E_i|\le\delta$ for every $i$, and $\sum_i|p_i-q_i|\le e^{2\delta}-1$.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete numbered argument is in items/thm-tdmath-finite-bath-error-bound.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Independent subsystem bulk limit
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let $\Omega_0$ be a nonempty finite set, let $E:\Omega_0\to\mathbb R$, and fix $\beta\in\mathbb R$. Define $Z_1=\sum_{i\in\Omega_0}e^{-\beta E_i}$ and the canonical law $q_i=e^{-\beta E_i}/Z_1$, and define $\bar E:=\sum_iq_iE_i$. For $N\ge1$, on $\Omega_0^N$ define $H_N(i_1,\ldots,i_N)=\sum_{k=1}^NE_{i_k}$. Give $\Omega_0^N$ the product probability law assigning $(i_1,\ldots,i_N)$ weight $\prod_{k=1}^Nq_{i_k}$, and define the $N$-subsystem partition sum $Z_N:=\sum_{(i_1,\ldots,i_N)\in\Omega_0^N}e^{-\beta H_N(i_1,\ldots,i_N)}$. Then $Z_N=Z_1^N$, $\mathbb E[H_N/N]=\bar E$, and $\operatorname{Var}(H_N/N)=\operatorname{Var}_q(E)/N$. Consequently, for every $\varepsilon>0$, $\mathbb P(|H_N/N-\bar E|\ge\varepsilon)\le\operatorname{Var}_q(E)/(N\varepsilon^2)$. If $\beta\ne0$, the mathematical free-energy density $-\beta^{-1}N^{-1}\log Z_N$ is exactly $-\beta^{-1}\log Z_1$ for every $N$.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete numbered argument is in items/thm-tdmath-independent-bulk-limit.md and its proof contract.

items.title: One-dimensional periodic Ising-chain limit
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Fix $\beta>0$ and $J,h\in\mathbb R$. For $N\ge2$, let $s_i\in\{-1,1\}$, $s_{N+1}=s_1$, $H_N(s)=-J\sum_{i=1}^Ns_is_{i+1}-h\sum_{i=1}^Ns_i$, and $Z_N=\sum_se^{-\beta H_N(s)}$. Define $\cosh x:=(e^x+e^{-x})/2$, $\sinh x:=(e^x-e^{-x})/2$, and $T_{s,t}:=e^{\beta Jst+\beta h(s+t)/2}$. Then $Z_N=\operatorname{tr}(T^N)=\lambda_+^N+\lambda_-^N$, where $\lambda_\pm=e^{\beta J}\cosh(\beta h)\pm\sqrt{e^{2\beta J}\sinh^2(\beta h)+e^{-2\beta J}}$ and $\lambda_+>|\lambda_-|$. Therefore $N^{-1}\log Z_N\to\log\lambda_+$. On every compact subset of $(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^2$ in $(\beta,J,h)$, the limit and its derivatives of every fixed finite order converge uniformly. This is a result for the specified one-dimensional periodic two-state model only.

items.title: Bounded finite-range lattice model
items.design_state: Draft definition carrier recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Fix integers $d\ge1$, $L\ge1$, a finite alphabet $\mathcal A$ of cardinality $q\ge1$, and a finite, possibly empty, list of interaction shapes $S_a\subset\mathbb Z^d$, each nonempty and contained in $[-R,R]^d$ for some integer $R\ge0$. $\|\Phi_a\|_\infty$ is finite because its domain is finite. For each shape let $\Phi_a:\mathcal A^{S_a}\to\mathbb R$ be a bounded interaction function. Set $J_0:=\sum_a\|\Phi_a\|_\infty$. On $\Lambda_L:=\{1,\ldots,L\}^d$, define the free-boundary energy $H_L(s):=\sum_a\sum_{x:x+S_a\subseteq\Lambda_L}\Phi_a((s_{x+u})_{u\in S_a})$, for configurations $s\in\mathcal A^{\Lambda_L}$. For $\beta>0$, define the finite partition sum $Z_L(\beta):=\sum_{s\in\mathcal A^{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_L(s)}$ and normalized log-partition density $p_L(\beta):=L^{-d}\log Z_L(\beta)$.

items.title: Finite-range lattice log-partition limit
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: For every fixed $\beta>0$, the sequence $p_L(\beta)$ of [[def-tdmath-bounded-finite-range-lattice]] has a finite limit as $L\to\infty$. If another finite-volume energy $\widetilde H_L$ on the same configurations satisfies $\sup_s|\widetilde H_L(s)-H_L(s)|\le C_bL^{d-1}$ for a constant $C_b$ independent of $L$, define $\widetilde Z_L(\beta):=\sum_{s\in\mathcal A^{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta\widetilde H_L(s)}$ and $\widetilde p_L(\beta):=L^{-d}\log\widetilde Z_L(\beta)$. Then $\widetilde p_L$ has the same limit. The result covers finite-alphabet, bounded, translation-invariant finite-range interactions on cubic boxes; it asserts no continuum-particle or long-range limit.

items.title: Limiting derivative and concentration
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: For the lattice models of [[thm-tdmath-finite-range-lattice-pressure-limit]], write $p_L(\gamma)=L^{-d}\log Z_L(\gamma)$ and let $p(\gamma)=\lim_Lp_L(\gamma)$ on an open interval $J\subseteq(0,\infty)$. At finite $L$, use the canonical law $\mathbb P_{\gamma,L}(s):=e^{-\gamma H_L(s)}/Z_L(\gamma)$ and its finite expectation $\mathbb E_{\gamma,L}$. If $p$ is differentiable at $\beta\in J$, then $\mathbb E_{\beta,L}[H_L]/L^d\to e:=-p'(\beta)$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are $c>0$ and $L_0$ such that for $L\ge L_0$, $\mathbb P_{\beta,L}(|H_L/L^d-e|\ge\varepsilon)\le2e^{-cL^d}$. No energy-density limit is asserted at a nondifferentiability point.

items.title: Finite ground-state degeneracy entropy limit
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let $I$ be a finite nonempty set, take the canonical model [[def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model]] on $J=(0,\infty)$, and let its energies be $E_i$ and positive weights be $g_i$. Write $E_0:=\min_{i\in I}E_i$, let $\mathcal G:=\{i\in I:E_i=E_0\}$ have cardinality $m\ge1$, and set $W_0:=\sum_{i\in\mathcal G}g_i$. As $\beta\to+\infty$, each ground-state probability tends to $g_i/W_0$ and each excited-state probability tends to zero. The Shannon entropy $H(p(\beta)):=-\sum_{i\in I}p_i(\beta)\log p_i(\beta)$ tends to $-\sum_{i\in\mathcal G}(g_i/W_0)\log(g_i/W_0)$. In particular, if all $g_i=1$, the ground-state probabilities tend to $1/m$ and the entropy tends to $\log m$. This is a finite-model statement only.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete numbered argument is in items/lem-tdmath-finite-ground-degeneracy.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Conditional entropy of finite memory given side information
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let $M$ and $R$ take values in finite sets under a joint probability law $p(m,r)\ge0$ with $\sum_{m,r}p(m,r)=1$. For any finite random variable $Y$ with law $p_Y$, define its Shannon entropy by $H(Y):=-\sum_{y:p_Y(y)>0}p_Y(y)\log p_Y(y)$; for a pair, $H(M,R)$ means this definition applied to its joint law. Put $a_r:=\sum_m p(m,r)$ and, when $a_r>0$, $q(m|r):=p(m,r)/a_r$. Thus $H(R)=-\sum_{r:a_r>0}a_r\log a_r$. Define $H(M|R):=\sum_{r:a_r>0}a_r[-\sum_{m:q(m|r)>0}q(m|r)\log q(m|r)]$. Then $H(M,R)=H(R)+H(M|R)$ and $H(M|R)\ge0$.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete numbered argument is in items/lem-tdmath-conditional-memory-entropy.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Mutual information of finite random variables
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: For finite random variables $M,R$ with joint law $p(m,r)$ and marginals $p_M,p_R$, use the entropy definition $H(Y)$ of [[lem-tdmath-conditional-memory-entropy]] for $Y=M,R,(M,R)$. Define $I(M;R):=\sum_{p(m,r)>0}p(m,r)\log\frac{p(m,r)}{p_M(m)p_R(r)}$. Then $I(M;R)=H(M)+H(R)-H(M,R)=H(M)-H(M|R)\ge0$, with equality exactly when $p(m,r)=p_M(m)p_R(r)$ for every pair.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete numbered argument is in items/lem-tdmath-mutual-information.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Trace-class Gibbs normalization for a semibounded self-adjoint operator
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $A$ be self-adjoint with regular Borel projection-valued measure $E$ from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], with $E((-\infty,a))=0$ for finite $a\in\mathbb R$. For each $\gamma>0$, define the bounded Gibbs operator $K_\gamma:=\Phi_E(f_\gamma)$ using the bounded Borel PVM integral of [[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]], where $f_\gamma(\lambda)=e^{-\gamma\lambda}$ for $\lambda\ge a$ and $f_\gamma(\lambda)=e^{-\gamma a}$ for $\lambda<a$. Fix $\beta>0$ and suppose $K_\beta$ is trace class in the sense of [[def-trace-class-operator]]. Then $K_\beta$ is injective and has a finite or countable orthonormal basis $(u_j)$ of $\mathcal H$ with $Au_j=E_ju_j$, $E_j\ge a$, and $K_\beta u_j=e^{-\beta E_j}u_j$. Its partition function $Z_\beta:=\operatorname{Tr}K_\beta=\sum_j e^{-\beta E_j}$ is positive and finite, and $\rho_\beta:=K_\beta/Z_\beta$ is positive with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho_\beta=1$. For every $B\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta B)=\sum_j(e^{-\beta E_j}/Z_\beta)\langle Bu_j,u_j\rangle$ absolutely. Further, let $J\subset(0,\infty)$ be open and suppose that for every compact $C\subset J$ there is a summable family $a_j\ge0$ with $(1+|E_j|^2)e^{-\gamma E_j}\le a_j$ for all $j$ and $\gamma\in C$. Then for each $\gamma\in J$, $K_\gamma$ is trace class with partition function $Z_\gamma:=\operatorname{Tr}K_\gamma=\sum_j e^{-\gamma E_j}$. With $p_j(\gamma):=e^{-\gamma E_j}/Z_\gamma$, define $\bar E_\gamma:=\sum_jp_j(\gamma)E_j$, $\operatorname{Var}_\gamma(E):=\sum_jp_j(\gamma)(E_j-\bar E_\gamma)^2$, and $S_\gamma:=-\sum_jp_j(\gamma)\log p_j(\gamma)$. These quantities are finite and satisfy $-\partial_\gamma\log Z_\gamma=\bar E_\gamma$, $\partial_\gamma^2\log Z_\gamma=\operatorname{Var}_\gamma(E)$, and $S_\gamma=\log Z_\gamma+\gamma\bar E_\gamma$ as in [[thm-tdmath-summable-canonical-differentiation]]. Countable nonnegative sums use the finite-subsum supremum convention of [[def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model]].
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete numbered argument is in items/thm-tdmath-general-trace-gibbs-model.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Grand-response derivatives are covariances
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $w:X\to[0,\infty)$ and $X_a:X\to\mathbb R$ ($1\le a\le r$) be measurable, and let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^r$ be open. For $\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r)$, define $\theta\cdot X(x):=\sum_{a=1}^r\theta_aX_a(x)$. Set $Z(\theta):=\int w\exp(\theta\cdot X)\,d\mu$ and assume $0<Z(\theta)<\infty$ on $U$. Suppose for every compact $K\subset U$ there is an integrable $G_K\ge0$ such that $w e^{\theta\cdot X}(1+\sum_a|X_a|^2)\le G_K$ pointwise for all $\theta\in K$. For the normalized density $p_\theta=w e^{\theta\cdot X}/Z(\theta)$, define $\mathbb E_\theta Y:=\int Yp_\theta\,d\mu$ when integrable and $\operatorname{Cov}_\theta(X_a,X_b):=\mathbb E_\theta[(X_a-\mathbb E_\theta X_a)(X_b-\mathbb E_\theta X_b)]$. Then $\partial_a\log Z=\mathbb E_\theta X_a$ and $\partial_b\mathbb E_\theta X_a=\operatorname{Cov}_\theta(X_a,X_b)$. Thus the Hessian of $\log Z$ is positive semidefinite. This is a mathematical model identity; it assumes no independence or absence of correlations.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete numbered argument is in items/thm-tdmath-grand-response-covariance.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Single-mode Bose and Fermi occupation fluctuations
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: For $q\in(0,1)$, the bosonic geometric law on $n\in\mathbb N_0$ with weights $(1-q)q^n$ has mean $q/(1-q)$ and variance $q/(1-q)^2=\mathbb E[n](1+\mathbb E[n])$; its relative standard deviation, defined as $\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(n)}/\mathbb E[n]$, tends to $1$ as $q\uparrow1$. The fermionic two-state law on $n\in\{0,1\}$ with weights $1/(1+q)$ and $q/(1+q)$ has mean $q/(1+q)$ and variance $q/(1+q)^2=\mathbb E[n](1-\mathbb E[n])$. Here Bose and Fermi name these explicitly specified counting laws; no claim about a physical preparation is made.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete numbered argument is in items/lem-tdmath-bose-fermi-mode-fluctuations.md and its proof contract.

items.title: Canonical mean and variance for a two-level system
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let the state set be $\{0,1\}$, with energies $E_0=0$, $E_1=\varepsilon>0$, unit weights, and $\beta>0$. Writing $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$, the excited-state probability is $q/(1+q)$, the mean energy is $\varepsilon q/(1+q)$, and the energy variance is $\varepsilon^2q/(1+q)^2>0$.

items.title: A perfectly correlated uniform pair has zero conditional entropy

items.title: A finite canonical law differs from a narrow-shell microcanonical law
items.design_state: Complete draft proof recorded; scoped checks and independent review remain pending.
items.statement: Let a two-state model have energies $0$ and $\varepsilon>0$, with unit state weights and $\beta>0$. Adopt the finite-shell convention that the microcanonical law is uniform over states whose energy lies in $[0,\Delta)$ when the shell is nonempty. For $0<\Delta<\varepsilon$, that shell contains only the ground state, whereas the canonical law assigns the excited state probability $e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon})>0$. Thus the two finite-ensemble laws differ.
items.strategy: proof_strategy: direct; complete numbered argument is in items/ex-tdmath-finite-ensemble-mismatch.md and its proof contract.
